\subsection*{Expanders --- Chernoff: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Concentration of visits to a set]
\lean{Expander.walk_visits_concentration}
\label{Expander.walk_visits_concentration}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.lambda, Expander.walkPMF}
Let $A$ be a symmetric stochastic matrix on a nonempty finite state space of size $n$,
and let $\lambda$ bound its operator norm on vectors orthogonal to the uniform vector,
with $0\leq\lambda\leq1$. Let $B$ be a set of states with $|B|=\beta n$, and let
$\delta>0$. For every $k\in\mathbb N$, the probability that the fraction of the $k+1$
visited states lying in $B$ differs from $\beta$ by more than $\delta$ is strictly less
than $2\exp\!\left(-\frac{(1-\lambda)\delta^2(k+1)}{60}\right)$.
\end{theorem}
